newsitem.title: INDIA: India and ASEAN must strengthen business ties.
newsitem.headline: India and ASEAN must strengthen business ties.

text.p: India and Southeast Asian nations should capitalise on existing trade and investment avenues to expand business, the secretary general of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) said on Monday.

"In view of our potential economic strengths, ASEAN and India must take advantage of each other's mutual complementarities and undertake measures to exploit trade and investment opportunities," Ajit Singh said.
Singh told a economic conference that ASEAN was confident of India's economic performance and looked to the year 2003, when ASEAN Free Trade Area (AFTA) would be fully implemented.
AFTA will allow ASEAN members to freely trade goods and services, he said.
"India's 'look east' policy and ASEAN's recent decision to elevate India to a full-dialogue partner status have contributed to a growing awareness," Singh said.
ASEAN's investment in India rose to 6.4 billion rupees ($179 million) in 1995 from 3.1 million in 1991, he said.
India launched sweeping economic reforms in 1991 under former Congress prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, after decades of socialist control, by liberalising industry and trade.
But Singh said that there was still a lack of information exchange between India and ASEAN, and inadequate physical infrastructure for business relationships to expand.
Singh praised Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda for reassuring foreign investors on the irreversibility of economic reforms.
Salman Khurshid, junior foreign minister in the previous Congress government, said that Deve Gowda's government must create a political consensus in India to carry-forward economic reforms.
